subject.title: feat: raise (or remove) 3-minute no-output watchdog cap on CLI requests

question: For ordinary inherited resumed CLI user runs with no explicit timeout intent, should OpenClaw keep the 180-second no-output guard, raise it to a longer bounded default, or support disabling it?
rationale: The source-level problem is real, but the remaining change intentionally trades faster stuck-process recovery for fewer false kills during legitimate long-silent work; automation should not choose that product/safety default.

options.title: Raise to a bounded longer default
options.body: Use a larger inherited-resume ceiling, keep positive per-backend overrides for stricter setups, and avoid adding a disable mode unless later evidence needs it.

options.title: Keep the 180-second guard
options.body: Document the current safety tradeoff and ask operators with known long-silent backends to configure backend-specific watchdog values.

options.title: Add an explicit disable mode
options.body: Allow `0` or `null` only with clear docs and tests proving the outer run timeout still protects users from unbounded stalls.

recommendation.title: Raise to a bounded longer default
recommendation.body: Use a larger inherited-resume ceiling, keep positive per-backend overrides for stricter setups, and avoid adding a disable mode unless later evidence needs it.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and verified the most recent merged timeout-provenance fix and explicitly preserved this inherited-resume guard in that work.
